entities.summary:
Hungary is a landlocked country in Central Europe, spanning much of the Carpathian Basin. It is bordered by Slovakia, Ukraine, Romania, Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, and Austria. With 10 million people and Budapest as its capital, Hungary occupies the historical heartland of the medieval Kingdom of Hungary — one of Central Europe's most powerful states from the year 1000 to the Ottoman conquest in 1526.

The Magyar tribes arrived in the Carpathian Basin around 895 CE under Árpád, establishing a nomadic confederation that King Stephen I (r. 1000–1038) transformed into a Christian kingdom organized on the Carolingian model. Medieval Hungary encompassed modern Slovakia, Croatia, Transylvania, and parts of Romania — a multi-ethnic kingdom that was one of the largest states in Europe. The Ottoman Battle of Mohács (1526) killed King Louis II and ended Hungarian independence for 400 years. Partition between Ottoman and Habsburg rule defined the next 150 years before Habsburg reunification (1699).

Hungary's 20th century was defined by trauma and transformation: World War I's Treaty of Trianon (1920) stripped two-thirds of its territory and half its population; the Communist period (1949–1989) included the Hungarian Revolution of 1956 — the most significant anti-Soviet uprising in the Eastern Bloc; and EU and NATO accession (2004) integrated Hungary into Western institutions. The Fidesz government under Viktor Orbán (2010–present) has generated sustained controversy over democratic backsliding.
